newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: KEDO awards Sept residual fuel between $115-$120/t.
newsitem.headline: KEDO awards Sept residual fuel between $115-$120/t.

text.p: The Korean Peninsular Energy Development Organisation (KEDO) has awarded its tender to buy 83,000 tonnes of residual fuel for September to two Japanese firms and a Dutch trader, industry officials said on Monday.
The cargoes were awarded between US$115-$120 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis to North Korea.
They said KEDO purchased 20,000 tonnes of residual fuel for delivery between Sept 5-10 from Dutch trader, Vitol.
It purchased another 20,000 tonnes from Japan's Mitsubishi Corp for delivery between Sept 25-30.
The remaining 43,000 tonnes was awarded to Itochu Corp for delivery between Sept 15-20, the sources said.
The cargoes will be delivered to the ports of Namp, Songrim or Sonbong, North Korea.
KEDO is an international organisation established to implement nuclear non-proliferation in North Korea and it has agreed to supply the country with 500,000 tonnes of fuel oil annually.
